ownership_reason: Only the gold reads the characters of the Option name: it rejects a name with a character that is not a Java identifier part, except that a single-character name may be ' ', '?' or '@', and then builds the Option. Hops 1-4 pass the name through unchanged and set independent properties (argument display name, long name, required flag, argument values, value separator, type) on the Option the gold returns; once the gold has thrown, no caller holds an Option to repair. The convention is pinned outside the gold: OptionValidator.validateOption (applied by every Option constructor) does the same step, and its javadoc lists it ('a single character opt that is either ' '(special case), '?', '@' or a letter'); the facade's javadoc refers the name rule to Option ('if opt is not a valid character. See Option.'); OptionBuilderTest.testIllegalOptions pins the rejection of '"' and of 'opt`' and the acceptance of 'opt'. The gold's javadoc promises an Option for every valid Option name, which '?' is. The facade body is one delegating call: the builder settings are private to OptionBuilder, so it passes them by value, and hop 1 restores the builder defaults through OptionBuilder.reset (made package-private, behaviour-preserving), before the Option is built, so the reset also happens when a name is rejected, as with the original finally block. In the correct configuration the gold applies exactly OptionValidator's rule before the constructor applies it again; the only observable difference from the original is the message text for an invalid name of two or more characters ('illegal option value' instead of 'opt contains illegal character value'), which no test or production code reads. Edits above the gold that pass the trigger replace the gold: building the Option directly with the Option constructor at a hop or the facade (the constructor's own check then stands in for the gold, whose result is discarded), or a pre-filter that builds single-character special names at a hop without calling the gold.
